summary: Folke Bergman worked in archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University and served as Amanuens of the East Asian collections at the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities from approximately 1935 to 1946.

Forbes Falconer specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Marischal College and the University of Aberdeen, and under Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, and Heinrich Ewald, before becoming Professor at University College London in 1834.

Forster Fitzgerald Arbuthnot worked in Indology. He studied at the East India Company College in 1851, served in the Indian Civil Service as Collector of Bombay City and Island (1853–1878), and founded the Kama Shastra Society.

Frances Wood specialized in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at North London Collegiate School, Newnham College, Cambridge, and Peking University, she held posts at the British Library (~1977–2013) and North Bristol NHS Trust (2023).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London and under Chögyam Trungpa between approximately 1971 and 1975.

Francesca Tarocco is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London in 2005, became a professor at Ca' Foscari University in 2016, and visited NYU Shanghai in 2017.

Francesco Adolfo Cannizzaro was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied under Angelo De Gubernatis (~1891–1893) and earned a degree in law from the University of Catania in 1894.

Francesco Cimmino was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin and University of Naples Federico II under Michele Kerbaker and Giovanni Flechia. He taught at Liceo Genovesi and was Professor of Sanskrit at Naples (1914–1935).

Francesco Lorenzo Pullè was an Indologist and linguist who studied under De Gubernatis, Weber, Mommsen, and Kiepert. He held professorships at the Universities of Padua (1875–1889), Pisa (1889–1899), and Bologna (1899–1925), and founded the Museo di Antichità Indiana.

Francesco Ribezzo worked in linguistics and archaeology. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Alfredo Trombetti, and at the universities of Naples and Leipzig. He later taught at Naples (1914–1921), Messina (1921–1925), and the University of Palermo (1925–1948).

Francesco Scerbo worked in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Seminario Vescovile di Nicastro and under Angelo De Gubernatis and Antelmo Severini, he held teaching posts in Hebrew at the University of Florence from 1892 and 1903 to 1924.

Francesco Sferra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having studied under Raffaele Torella (~1990–1999). He has held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", University of Naples Federico II, the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and Series Minor.

Linguist Francis A. Wood studied at Northwestern University, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Chicago. He held professorships at Chaddock College (1890–1893), Cornell College (1897–1903), and the University of Chicago (1903–1927).

Francis Balfour was active in Indology. He earned his Dr.Med. from the University of Edinburgh in 1767 and served as an assistant surgeon and full surgeon in the East India Company between 1769 and 1807.

Francis Brandt worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Brasenose College, Oxford (~1858–1870), he served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1889) and was Lecturer in Tamil and Indian Law at the University of Cambridge (1891–1895).
Francis Brinkley, who worked in Japanology, studied at Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo between approximately 1878 and 1881.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton was a physician and researcher in history and archaeology who studied under John Hope at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin was a scholar in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was a co-founder of The Asiatic Society in 1784 and became the first Professor of Persian at Fort William College in 1801.

Francis Harold Cook specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After completing his doctoral thesis at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1987) and chaired the Numata Center and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.
Francis John Monahan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1883 and joined the Indian Civil Service as a civil servant in 1885.
